name: wifi security
pitch: Help the person lock down their home wifi and router settings to stop unauthorised access.
instructions: Start by asking the person which router they use, or if they have the manual handy. If they do not know, ask them to find the router's IP address (usually printed on a sticker underneath) and type it into a web browser. When the router login page appears, ask the person for the username and password. If they have never changed these, suggest common defaults such as admin/admin or admin/password, but tell them to check the manual first. Once logged in, look for a section labelled Wireless, Wi‑Fi, or Network. Change the wifi network name (SSID) to something that does not reveal the person's identity or location. Set the security mode to WPA2‑PSK or WPA3 if available. Create a strong password of at least 12 characters mixing letters, numbers and symbols. If the router offers a guest network, enable it and give it a separate name and password. If any setting is greyed out or the person does not recognise a field, stop and ask them before changing anything. When the changes are saved, take a screenshot of the final settings page and use make_page to create a short summary for the person, listing the new network name, the security type and the password. If the router firmware is out of date, tell the person they can check the manufacturer's website for an update, but do not download or install it without their say‑so. If the person gets stuck at any point, stop and use request_help to ask them for the needed information or permission.

skills.name: check-router-settings
skills.description: Guide the person through changing wifi and router security settings.
skills.body: 1. Ask the person for the router's make and model, or if they can find the IP address and login details. 2. If they have the details, navigate to the router's web page using browser_navigate. 3. Use browser_type to enter the username and password. 4. Use browser_click to open the wireless or wifi section. 5. Use browser_type to change the network name (SSID) to a neutral name. 6. Use browser_type to set the security mode to WPA2‑PSK or WPA3 and enter a strong password. 7. If a guest network option appears, enable it and set a separate name and password. 8. Use browser_click to save or apply the changes. 9. Take a snapshot of the final page with browser_snapshot. 10. Use make_page to write a short summary for the person with the new network name, security type and password. 11. If any step fails or the person is unsure, stop and ask them before continuing.

readme:
# wifi security

Lock down your home wifi and router so only trusted devices can join. The bot will guide you to change the network name, security type and password, and will give you a summary page at the end. It will never change anything without your say‑so.
